hints.func-sumifs: SUMIF takes one condition. Two of them need SUMIFS, and SUMIFS puts the sum range first.

hints.value: Only two shipped orders clear 200, at 320 and 300, which total 620.

docs.explain:
SUMIFS adds the cells in one range whose rows meet every condition you set. It takes the range to add first, then pairs of range and condition. That is the opposite order to SUMIF, and the reason a SUMIF habit gets it wrong.

Here the sum range is C2:C6, the region must read North and the rep must read Ada. Rows 2 and 6 match, so the answer is 720. The second screen drops the rep and adds an amount above 200, which leaves out the shipped order at 180 and gives 620.

Every criteria range has to be the same shape as the sum range, or the rows drift and the total is quietly wrong. Text and comparisons both go in quotes, and wildcards work inside them. A condition that needs OR across two columns takes two SUMIFS calls added together.

errors.text: A criteria range is a different shape from the sum range, so the rows no longer line up. Every range in the call has to start and end on the same rows.
The function is typed as SUMIF, which takes its arguments in another order: range, condition, sum range.
SUMIFS joins conditions with AND. Two conditions on the same column can never both match, and the answer comes back as 0.

docs.atWork: A sales sheet totalling one rep in one region, and an order book totalling the shipped orders above a credit limit.
docs.outcome: Total the rows that meet two conditions at once instead of filtering the table first.
docs.teaches: SUMIFS with two condition pairs, text and comparison criteria
docs.dataset: Repo sales by region and shipped orders by value

seo.title: SUMIFS in Excel: two conditions at once
seo.description: Most real totals ask two questions. SUMIFS takes the range to add first, then a range and a condition for each. Get that order wrong and the total drifts.
